# `tool-name-style`

**Tool rule** · `warning` · **off by default**, enable it to use it

Tool names follow the project's naming convention: one style, optionally a prefix.

A tool rule judges one tool from its own definition, so it runs everywhere: `lint()`, `lintTools()`, the CLI, the Playwright fixture, the audit crawler and the ESLint plugin.

## Options

| Option   | Default        |
| -------- | -------------- |
| `style`  | `"snake_case"` |
| `prefix` | `""`           |

## Configuring it

```ts
lint(snapshot, { rules: { "tool-name-style": false } }); // off
lint(snapshot, { rules: { "tool-name-style": "warning" } }); // change severity
lint(snapshot, { rules: { "tool-name-style": { style: "snake_case" } } });
```

```bash
npx @swissspidy/webmcp-lint tools.json --rule tool-name-style=off
```

```js
// eslint.config.js
{ rules: { "webmcp/tool-name-style": "error" } }
```
